clue.text: English aristocrat's short sword

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: standard abbreviation for English
an aristocrat is a peer; the 's stands for 'is', and the peer is short of its last letter

explanation.surface: A British nobleman carries a small sword at his side.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'is': the aristocrat is short, so PEER loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing weapon, a thrusting sword with a stiff blade.

clue.text: Sharp boss, LSD user

parts.note: acid in the sense of sharp or biting
a head is the boss of an organisation

explanation.surface: A cutting manager turns out to be dropping LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for LSD, and an acidhead is a habitual taker of the drug.

clue.text: Takes a siesta, then son shaves when up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: standard abbreviation for son
to peel is to shave off a thin outer layer

explanation.surface: Someone naps after lunch, and then their son has a shave on getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of S plus PEELS is turned upside down in the column, giving SLEEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, so someone taking one sleeps.

clue.text: Nutty, it is a rum dessert

indicators.note: nutty means crazy, so these letters go wild and rearrange

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pudding with nuts in it, laced with rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nutty' poses as a description of the dessert; it signals the rearrangement. Rum, too, is fodder, not the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone.

clue.text: Nobleman in fear, lately

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A peer who has recently become frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking between marquess and viscount.

clue.text: European, small Parisienne, appearing in Czech play, will get a coach

indicators.note: things appearing in a play are placed inside it

parts.note: R.U.R. is Karel Čapek's play that introduced the word robot; it is the outer piece
standard abbreviation for European
petite is French for small, in its feminine form

explanation.surface: A small Frenchwoman cast in a Czech drama is given a tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) is the Czech play, and it splits around the other pieces; 'Parisienne' tells you to use the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A répétiteur is a vocal coach who rehearses opera singers, a sense of coaching or tutoring.

clue.text: A chopped pungent relish

indicators.note: something chopped has a piece cut off its end

parts.note: taken as written
spicy, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A finely cut spicy condiment for the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopped' looks like kitchen work on the relish; it trims the word for pungent.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly served alongside meats, loosely an accompaniment or relish.

clue.text: Saying one with rock group learns meeting knight, old racing driver

parts.note: a member of the rock band the Rolling Stones
to gather is to learn or infer
N is the chess notation for a knight
standard abbreviation for old
Stirling Moss, the British Formula One driver

explanation.surface: A rock musician is introduced to a knighted veteran racing driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Sir Stirling Moss himself, but 'knight' and 'old' each give one letter, N and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb is a saying: someone always on the move never accumulates anything.

clue.text: Gag Daniel cracked failed completely

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so its letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian's joke about Daniel bombed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's comedy flop matches the definition neatly; 'cracked' suits jokes and eggs alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay an egg is an idiom for a performance flopping completely.

clue.text: See 7
Late extra expected

parts.note: over means extra, left in excess
due means expected to arrive

explanation.surface: An extra item that was expected late.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has not arrived by the time it was expected, so it is late.

clue.text: Complaint got from working in metal

indicators.note: letters that are working are being worked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A metalworker has picked up an industrial illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint, in the medical sense, is an illness or ailment.

clue.text: Newspaper articles with it must give guidance

parts.note: leaders are a newspaper's editorial articles
with it means fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: Editorials that are trendy ought to provide direction.
explanation.walkthrough: In British papers a leader is the main editorial opinion piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is the act of directing others, which is guidance.

clue.text: Vegetables popular in French taverns

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: auberges are French inns; this is the outer piece
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Eggplants are a favourite dish in French inns.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergines are the British name for eggplants, purple-skinned vegetables.

clue.text: Very much similar to Charles Pooter's profession?

parts.note: like means similar to
Pooter is the Nobody of The Diary of a Nobody, so his trade is a nobody's business

explanation.surface: Asking whether a job resembles that of the Grossmiths' famous clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Pooter is the self-important City clerk of George and Weedon Grossmith's comic novel The Diary of a Nobody; the question mark flags the playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom like nobody's business means intensely or to an extraordinary degree, which is very much.

clue.text: See 14
Caledonian company in street with small staff

indicators.note: in says the first piece is set inside the second

parts.note: standard abbreviation for street; the outer piece
standard abbreviation for company
standard abbreviation for small
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A Scottish firm based on a high street with only a few employees.
explanation.walkthrough: S(CO)T then S and MAN. Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonian as a noun means a native of Scotland, a Scotsman.

clue.text: Embarrassed American kept secret

indicators.note: someone embarrassed is flustered and disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A red-faced American kept the matter quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase for proceedings held in private, kept from the public.

clue.text: Active agent trapping head of ring

indicators.note: trapping means holding something inside

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy; the outer piece

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of ring

explanation.surface: An operative captures the leader of a spy ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means lively and nimble, especially of an older person, so active.

clue.text: Carmen and Loot performed in Riviera resort

indicators.note: a work performed is put on in a new version, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged; 'and' only joins them

explanation.surface: Bizet's opera and Joe Orton's play staged on the Côte d'Azur.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo is the casino district of Monaco on the French Riviera coast.

clue.text: Was first killed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: came top, headed a list
second meaning: slang for put to death

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one person's grim fate; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To top is both to come first and, informally, to kill someone.

clue.text: Drugs ape so it relaxes

indicators.note: letters that relax loosen out of their set order and settle differently

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Narcotics calm a monkey down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relaxes' fits the surface as the drugs' effect; it is the rearranging signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotics derived from opium, a class of drugs.

clue.text: Express disapproval over leader of union in a short skirt

parts.note: tut is a sound of disapproval

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of union

explanation.surface: A trade unionist frowns upon a skimpy skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is a ballerina's short stiff skirt.

clue.text: A pepper pot I cooked — chaps tucked in

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or tampered with, so the letters are reworked
things tucked in are placed inside something else

parts.note: these letters rearranged; the outer piece
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A cook prepares a pot of peppers, and the men tuck into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'tucked in' mean eating; here it means placed inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimento is a sweet red pepper, also called a pimiento.

clue.text: Fleet vehicle turned up close to Piccadilly

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of Piccadilly

explanation.surface: A quick car pulls up near Piccadilly in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like an adjective for fast; it is the noun for ships. Piccadilly is a main street in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A navy is a nation's fleet of warships.

clue.text: Turn out in uniform attending first showing of Utrillo in gallery

parts.note: even means uniform, level

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery; the outer piece

indicators.note: the first showing of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of Utrillo

explanation.surface: Someone in uniform turns up for the opening of a Utrillo show at a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: EVEN then T(U)ATE. 'Uniform' is not clothing here but evenness; the Tate is a famous London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is to result or happen in the end, which is to turn out.

clue.text: Wanders right away from Blackburn, say

indicators.note: a letter that goes away from a word is taken out of it

parts.note: Blackburn Rovers is an English football club, so Rovers is an example of Blackburn
standard abbreviation for right; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A walker heads off rightwards out of the Lancashire town of Blackburn.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackburn Rovers is a Lancashire football club; ROVERS minus one R.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to roam about aimlessly, so roves means wanders.
